title: JLPT N5 — Complete Foundations
description: Greetings, family, numbers, time, food, shopping, daily verbs, particles, adjectives, and directions.

units.title: First Steps & Greetings
units.subtitle: あいさつ · Polite greetings, gratitude & farewells

lessons.title: Morning to Night Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet people politely at any time of day.
lessons.grammarNote: Japanese greetings shift by time of day. Adding ございます raises formality.

example.term: 先生、おはようございます。
こんにちは、お元気ですか。
こんばんは、寒いですね。
example.translation: Good evening, it's cold isn't it?

example.term: おやすみなさい、また明日。
お久しぶりです。お元気ですか。
example.translation: Long time no see. How are you?

lessons.title: Gratitude & Apologies
lessons.objective: Thank others, apologize, and ask politely.
lessons.grammarNote: すみません covers 'Excuse me', 'I'm sorry', and politely calling a waiter.

items.term: ありがとうございます
items.reading: ありがとうございます

example.term: 教えてくれてありがとうございます。
example.translation: Thank you very much for telling me.

example.term: —ありがとうございます。—どういたしまして。
すみません、駅はどこですか。
example.transliteration: Sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka.
example.translation: Excuse me, where is the station?

example.term: コーヒーをお願いします。

lessons.title: Yes, No & Farewells
lessons.grammarNote: Use また明日 (see you tomorrow) for friends and 失礼します when leaving an office.

example.term: 手伝いましょうか。いいえ、大丈夫です。
example.translation: Shall I help? No, I'm fine.

units.title: Introductions & Family
units.subtitle: じこしょうかいとかぞく · Talking about yourself, people & family

lessons.title: Self-Introductions
lessons.objective: Introduce your name and background politely.
lessons.grammarNote: Particle は (pronounced 'wa') marks the topic. End polite identity statements with です.

example.term: はじめまして、マヘシュです。
example.translation: Nice to meet you, I'm Mahesh.

items.term: よろしくお願いします
items.reading: よろしくおねがいします

example.term: どうぞよろしくお願いします。

lessons.title: People & Occupations
lessons.objective: Refer to teachers, students, friends, and coworkers.
lessons.grammarNote: Attach さん (-san) after other people's names, never after your own name.

example.term: 山田先生は優しいです。

example.transliteration: Watashi wa daigaku no gakusei desu.

example.translation: My father is a company employee.

example.transliteration: Ano hito wa dare desu ka.

lessons.title: My Family
lessons.objective: Talk about family members using humble family words.
lessons.grammarNote: Japanese uses different words for your own family (母 haha) vs. someone else's family (お母さん okaasan).

example.translation: There are four people in my family.

example.transliteration: Chichi wa ryouri ga tokui desu.
example.translation: My father is good at cooking.
I talked on the phone with my mother.

example.term: 兄は東京に住んでいます。
example.transliteration: Ani wa Toukyou ni sunde imasu.
example.translation: My older brother lives in Tokyo.
My younger sister is a high school student.

units.title: Numbers, Time & Calendar
units.subtitle: すうじとじかん · Counting, hours, and days of the week

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 10
lessons.objective: Read and pronounce essential Sino-Japanese numbers.
lessons.grammarNote: Combine tens and ones cleanly: 12 is 十二 (juu-ni), 25 is 二十五 (ni-juu-go).

lessons.title: Higher Numbers & Prices
lessons.objective: Handle tens, hundreds, and yen prices.
lessons.grammarNote: Attach 円 (en) to numbers for Japanese yen: 百円 (100 yen), 千円 (1,000 yen).

example.term: 百円ショップで買いました。
example.translation: I bought it at a 100-yen shop.

lessons.title: Days & Calendar
lessons.objective: Refer to yesterday, today, tomorrow, and days of the week.
lessons.grammarNote: Days of the week end in 曜日 (youbi): 月曜日 (Monday), 日曜日 (Sunday).

example.term: 今日はいい天気ですね。
example.transliteration: Kyou wa ii tenki desu ne.

example.term: 毎日日本語を勉強します。

example.translation: I watch a movie on the weekend.

units.title: Food, Cafés & Shopping
units.subtitle: たべものとかいもの · Ordering meals and buying items

lessons.title: Drinks & Everyday Food
lessons.objective: Name staple Japanese foods and drinks.
lessons.grammarNote: Add お (o-) before polite food nouns like お茶 (ocha, tea) and お水 (omizu, water).

example.term: 朝ご飯を食べましたか。

example.transliteration: Shinsen na sakana ga suki desu.

lessons.title: At the Restaurant
lessons.objective: Order politely and compliment your meal.
lessons.grammarNote: Say いただきます before eating and ごちそうさまでした after finishing a meal.

example.term: このラーメンはおいしいです。

items.translation: Thank you for the meal (before eating)

example.translation: Let's eat / Thank you for this meal!

example.term: すみません、お会計をお願いします。
今日のおすすめは何ですか。
example.transliteration: Kyou no osusume wa nan desu ka.

lessons.title: Shopping & Prices
lessons.objective: Ask prices and choose items in a store.
lessons.grammarNote: Use これ (this near me), それ (that near you), あれ (that over there).

example.term: スーパーの野菜は安いです。
example.transliteration: Suupaa no yasai wa yasui desu.

example.translation: It's a bit expensive, isn't it?

units.title: Daily Verbs & Core Particles
units.subtitle: どうしとじょし · Polite -ます verbs and sentence particles

lessons.title: Action Verbs (-ます)
lessons.objective: Describe everyday routines in polite form.
lessons.grammarNote: Polite verbs end in ます (present/future), ません (negative), ました (past).

example.term: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。

example.translation: I read a book at night.

example.term: 漢字をノートに書きます。
example.translation: I write kanji in a notebook.

lessons.title: Going, Coming & Returning
lessons.objective: Talk about movement with に and へ.
lessons.grammarNote: Mark destinations with に or へ, and mode of transport with で (電車で = by train).

example.translation: My friend is coming to my house.

lessons.title: Places & Transit
lessons.objective: Combine places with で (where an action happens) and に (existence).
lessons.grammarNote: Use で where an action occurs (学校で勉強します) and に where something exists (机の上に本があります).

example.term: バスで学校へ行きます。
example.translation: I go to school by bus.

example.term: 図書館で本を借ります。
example.translation: I borrow a book at the library.

example.term: 電車は速くて便利です。

units.title: Adjectives, Weather & Directions
units.subtitle: けいようしとてんき · Describing things and asking where

lessons.title: I-Adjectives
lessons.objective: Describe size, age, and speed with い-adjectives.
lessons.grammarNote: To make an い-adjective negative, change final い to くない (大きい → 大きくない).

example.term: 大きい公園があります。
小さい猫がかわいいです。
新しいアプリを作ります。
京都には古いお寺が多いです。
example.transliteration: Kyouto ni wa furui otera ga ooi desu.

example.term: 新幹線はとても速いです。
example.translation: The bullet train is very fast.

lessons.title: Na-Adjectives
lessons.objective: Modify nouns with な-adjectives like 静かな and 便利な.
lessons.grammarNote: Add な when placing a な-adjective directly before a noun: 静かな町 (a quiet town).

example.term: ここは静かな場所です。
example.transliteration: Koko wa shizuka na basho desu.
Eki no chikaku wa benri desu.

example.term: 桜がとてもきれいです。
example.translation: The cherry blossoms are very pretty.

example.term: 富士山は有名な山です。
example.transliteration: Fujisan wa yuumei na yama desu.
example.translation: Mt. Fuji is a famous mountain.

lessons.title: Weather & Essential Questions
lessons.objective: Talk about weather and ask basic survival questions.
lessons.grammarNote: Add か to the end of a polite sentence to form a question without changing word order.

example.term: 今日の天気は晴れです。
example.transliteration: Kyou no tenki wa hare desu.

example.term: すみません、分かりません。
右に曲がってください。
